content.short: ERC721A is a gas-efficient implementation of the ERC721 standard that enables batch minting of multiple tokens.
content.description: ERC721A is a gas-efficient implementation of the ERC721 standard designed for batch minting of multiple NFTs. Created by the Chiru Labs Azuki team, this Solidity contract lets developers specify how many tokens to mint in a single transaction, enabling large-scale mints with reduced gas costs. It also supports forking the repository to add features or customize behavior as needed, helping projects tailor the contract to their minting workflows while staying aligned with the original design.

resources.title: Where the Gas Savings Come From
resources.tldr: Minting one NFT costs 154,814 gas the old way and 76,690 here. Minting five saves over seven times. The mechanism behind that.

resources.title: The Three Optimisations Azuki Made
resources.tldr: Redesigned storage layout and ownership updated once per batch rather than per token. Plus the assumptions that buys.
